title: security: enforce RBAC v2 KMS region residency + audit logging enhancements
author: Ava Patel
description:
Motivation: customers in regulated industries require strict KMS residency controls and end-to-end audit trails for key usage. This PR moves RBAC v2 KMS region pinning from audit-only to an enforceable policy mode and enriches audit logs with KMS metadata needed for post-facto compliance checks.

What I changed (summary):
- Add a new enforcement path in the RBAC v2 policy evaluator that rejects create/update requests for encryption keys or resources that reference KMS keys located outside allowed regions for the account/tenant.
- Enrich audit logs with kms.key_id, kms.key_region and policy_enforcement.result fields for every call that touches encrypted artifacts.
- Introduce a feature flag (security.rbac_v2.kms_region_residency.enforce) defaulting to disabled for canary rollout.
- Add migration tooling to backfill existing resources and surface violations via the compliance dashboard.
- Tests: unit + integration tests against a local KMS emulator and end-to-end compliance smoke tests.

Implementation notes:
- Policy evaluator: added a KmsResidencyEnforcer that hooks into the existing RBAC v2 evaluation pipeline. It queries account residency config and cross-checks the kms key region embedded in the request (validated via signer header). Errors return a 403 with a machine-readable code (RBAC_KMS_REGION_VIOLATION).
- Audit logging: audit events now include an optional kms object {key_id, key_region} and a policy_enforcement object {policy_id, result, reason}. This is serialized as part of our structured-audit payload and forwarded to the audit-log-exporter with the same retention rules.
- Backfill: small migration that scans resources in the account, checks key regions, and writes a compliance_report entry for each violation. Backfill is idempotent and safe to run multiple times.
- Config & rollout: gated behind feature flag with a staged rollout plan (internal-only -> beta customers -> GA). Ops playbook added in the runbook folder.

Checklist: 
- [x] New enforcer implemented and wired into the evaluator
- [x] Structured audit enrichment added
- [x] Migration/backfill tooling included
- [x] Unit & integration tests added
- [x] Docs and runbook for rollout included

Related: ENG-4589, ENG-4620, SUP-1324. See internal runbook link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4589/kms-region-residency-enforcement (internal).

review_comments: Marcus Chen (reviewer): Please make sure the enforcer only runs after signature validation - otherwise attackers could spoof kms metadata. Also add a small perf benchmark for the evaluator path.
Ava Patel (author): Good call - I added signer verification before the residency check and included a micro-benchmark in tests/integration. See commit b9f3a11.
Lina Gomez (reviewer): Audit payload size looks ok, but ensure we keep elasticity for downstream exporters; added a nit to avoid embedding large key metadata blobs.
Ava Patel (author): Addressed - audit formatter now truncates non-essential key metadata and only sends key_id and key_region. Updated structured_formatter.go accordingly.
Diego Alvarez (SRE): What is the rollout plan? Will we alert on violations in audit-only mode?

Ava Patel (author): Rollout plan is in docs/runbooks/kms-region-residency-enforcement.md. In audit-only mode we create compliance_report entries and emit high-severity alerts for new violations in the first 48 hours to the compliance channel.
